newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on exports, wheat, soy gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on exports, wheat, soy gains.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher with fresh bullish input coming from the export sector plus strong gains in wheat and soybeans, traders said.
"Cold weather helped out and we had good ex port inspections," one trader noted.
USDA early Monday said 48.376 million bushels of corn were inspected for export during the week ended December 12, above trade estimates for 40 million to 45 million bushels.
Slow farmer selling and mostly firm cash basis markets also were supportive, the traders said.
Cold weather in the U.S. Midwest which likely will boost feed consumption by livestock also was contributed to the advances as did the posting of no deliveries against the December contract.
Forecasters Monday said frigid cold will blanket the United States from the Rocky Mountains to the Appalachians this week with sub-zero temperatures extending into Texas.
Corn futures closed unchanged to 2-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with December up 2-3/4 at $2.70 a bushel. March was up 3/4 at $2.63-1/2.
Technicians cited first resistance in March corn at $2.64 per bushel and second resistance at $2.66. The session high for March was $2.64.
First support in the March was at $2.62 and second support was at $2.60. The session low for March was $2.61-3/4.
Rosenthal Collins bought two million bushels of March and sold two million May and Refco Inc bought 1.5 million each of March and July and sold three million March, the traders said.
Cargill Inc bear spread two million bushels of March/December.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 47,000 contracts, above the 42,147 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Smith Barney bought 400 July $3.20 puts at 54-1/4 cents and bought 400 May $3.20 puts at 55 cents but sold 400 May $2.60 puts at 7-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, above the 9,111 traded Friday.
